title: Toward Energy-Efficient and Low-Power Arrhythmia Detection for Wearable Devices
abstract: arXiv:2607.14747v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death worldwide, and conditions such as arrhythmia often require long-term monitoring for effective detection and diagnosis. However, current wearable monitoring devices are bulky, uncomfortable, and typically rely on clinicians to manually evaluate electrocardiograms (ECGs). While Deep Learning (DL) algorithms have shown superior performance in arrhythmia detection and classification, their computational complexity coupled with high power consumption limit deployment in wearable devices. To address this challenge, this paper investigates the use of approximation techniques to reduce the power and energy consumption of DL architectures while maintaining acceptable classification performance. translated_title: 面向可穿戴设备的低功耗高能效心律失常检测
translated_abstract: 心血管疾病是全球主要的死亡原因，诸如心律失常等病症通常需要长期监测才能实现有效的检测和诊断。然而，目前的可穿戴监测设备体积庞大、佩戴不舒适，且通常依赖临床医生手动评估心电图（ECG）。虽然深度学习（DL）算法在心律失常检测和分类方面展现出卓越的性能，但其计算复杂性和高功耗限制了其在可穿戴设备上的部署。为了应对这一挑战，本文研究了利用近似技术来降低深度学习架构的功耗和能量消耗，同时保持可接受的分类性能。具体而言，在一个最先进的深度学习模型及其相应的硬件架构中，研究了数据精度降低和近似乘法等技术。
tldr: 本文通过在深度学习心律失常检测模型及其硬件架构中采用数据精度降低和近似乘法等近似技术，在保持可接受分类精度的同时显著降低了功耗与能耗，使检测系统能够高效部署于可穿戴设备。
en_tdlr: This paper employs approximation techniques such as data precision reduction and approximate multiplication in a state-of-the-art DL model and its hardware architecture, significantly reducing power and energy consumption while maintaining acceptable classification performance for wearable arrhythmia detection.
